Apply the Template of a Journal to a Plot

Source: R/journals.R
apply_journal.Rd

Adds the theme of a journal, journal_theme(), and its palette to a plot, as apply_theme_set() does for a theme set.

Usage

apply_journal(plot, journal = "nature", palette = NULL, markdown = FALSE)

Arguments

plot

A ggplot object.

journal

The id of a journal (see journal_templates()), or a template made by journal_template().

palette

The name of a color scale set to use instead of the palette of the journal (see list_color_scales()), for example "okabe_ito". NA keeps the colors of the plot and adds only the theme, which is what you want for a continuous color scale.

markdown

Passed on to journal_theme(): TRUE renders markdown in the titles, the x axis title, the legend title and the strips.

Value

A ggplot object.

See also

compare_journals() to see one plot in several journals.

Examples

library(ggplot2)
od <- subset(example_growth(), measure == "OD600")
p <- ggplot(od, aes(time, value, color = strain)) +
  geom_line() +
  labs(x = "Incubation time (hr)", y = "OD600", color = NULL)

apply_journal(p, "science")


# the same plot with the Okabe-Ito palette
apply_journal(p, "science", palette = "okabe_ito")
